text: Counter tallies anything countable, and it does it in one line.
It lives in collections, alongside the other specialised containers.
It's the one-line answer to counting words, votes, or anything else that repeats.
We split a sentence into words, giving us a list with repeats.
Passing that list to Counter counts every element as it goes.
Printing it shows each word with its tally, ordered most common first.
You index it like a dictionary, because a Counter is a dictionary underneath.
Red appears three times, so counts of red gives three.
Most common one gives you the single biggest entry, as a list of pairs.
Pass a bigger number and you get that many of the top entries back.
Update adds more items to the existing tally rather than replacing it.
Blue was two, we added two more, and now it's four.
